sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who is the user, what is the job, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: States the user and the job in one sentence
Derives turns per month and peak turns per second from the 60,000 conversations
Names a success metric with a target, paired with a wrong-refund guard metric
Lists at least one thing explicitly out of scope

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the system as layers: what runs in each, what it hands to the next, and why it exists.
criteria: Has separate layers for orchestration, retrieval, tools and guardrails
Shows that the customer, not the model, confirms a refund
States one idea that separates what the model decides from what code decides

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: Which sources feed the agent, how fresh does each need to be, and how does each reach the model?
criteria: Reads orders and payments live through tools instead of indexing them
Gives policy articles a sync trigger (webhook or schedule) with a freshness target
Keeps internal-only playbook text out of what customers are shown

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How do policy pages become retrievable, citable chunks, and how do edits flow through?
criteria: Chunks by heading or section with a stated token size
Attaches metadata used later (article id, section, region or updated date)
Re-embeds only changed chunks using a content hash
Estimates embedding cost or corpus size in tokens

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: What is the agent's control flow, and what makes it stop?
criteria: Uses a fixed graph or workflow with routing in code, not a free planner
Names a step limit and a time limit with numbers
Executes a refund only after an explicit customer confirmation
Defines when the agent hands off to a human

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What does the agent remember within a conversation and across conversations, and where?
criteria: Separates turn, thread and customer memory with a store and an expiry for each
Checkpoints state so a crash mid-refund resumes rather than restarts
Keeps per-customer data out of the cached prompt prefix

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: Which tools does the agent get, with what arguments, and what does each enforce?
criteria: Lists each tool with its arguments and whether it reads or writes
Takes the customer id from the verified session, not from a model argument
Computes the refund amount server-side rather than accepting it from the model
Uses an idempotency key on the refund call

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What is the API surface, and how is the latency budget spent?
criteria: Streams responses (SSE or WebSocket) and supports resume after a dropped connection
Splits the time-to-first-token budget by stage and the total fits 1.5 s
Puts refund confirmation on a route the model cannot call
Verifies webhook signatures

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What do you cache, what do you never cache, and what does it do to cost?
criteria: Orders the prompt stable-first with a cache breakpoint
Shows a per-turn cost and a monthly cost with and without the prompt cache
States that refund and eligibility results are never cached
Takes a position on a semantic answer cache with a reason

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Which stores hold what, how big are they, and why these?
criteria: Names each store with what it holds and a size estimate
Keeps a local refund ledger with uniqueness constraints
Justifies the vector store choice with a measured number (recall or latency)
States retention for transcripts

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What shapes does the agent return, and which parts come from the model versus the system?
criteria: Defines typed output shapes beyond free text (proposal, receipt, handoff)
Renders refund amounts and receipts from tool results, never from model text
Specifies what the human receives on handoff

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: For each rule that protects money, data or trust, what enforces it if the model ignores its instructions?
criteria: Enforces per-order and per-customer refund caps in code
Treats pasted text and order notes as untrusted data
Checks answers against cited chunks before or while streaming
Keeps card data and PII out of the model and the logs

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: What business number moves, and how do you prove the agent caused it?
criteria: Gives baseline and target for the headline metric
Uses a holdout or A/B split to attribute impact
Defines resolved in a way that excludes abandoned chats (for example a reopen window)
Translates the result into dollars or hours

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, and what catches each failure?
criteria: Covers a payment timeout with an idempotent retry
Covers a model provider outage with a fallback
Covers a retrieval miss with abstention and handoff
Names an alert or kill switch for at least one failure

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it, and what number unlocks each step?
criteria: Builds the eval set before features
Ends each step with a measurable number
Ships refunds last, first with human approval, then behind a flag or canary
